title: arcosian common definitions
description: Shared $defs for the arcosian ontology. Not a document type: other schemas reference these shapes as "common.schema.json#/$defs/<name>". Changing a shape here changes every document that uses it, so keep edits backward compatible within schema_version 1.0.
$comment: Ontology version 1.0. Loops are graphs of steps; parameters are tunable numbers with ranges; mechanics bind verbs to rules. See skill game-ontology for the conceptual model.

schema_version.description: Ontology schema version. Every top-level arcosian document carries "1.0"; tools refuse documents from a future major version instead of guessing.

schema_name.description: Optional self-identification of the document type (a canonical schema name such as "level-spec"). validate_json.py --auto uses it when the file name does not follow the naming conventions.

id.description: Stable identifier: starts with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, '_', '.', ':' or '-', at most 128 characters. Prefer lower snake_case ("merge_two", "core", "coins"). Ids are referenced from other documents, so never rename one casually.

id_list.description: Unique list of ids referring to objects defined elsewhere (verbs, mechanics, resources, assets).

feature_id.description: Feature identifier: 'F' followed by 3 or 4 digits (F001 to F9999). Matches features.json and .gamestudio/evidence/<FEATURE-ID>/.

slug.description: URL- and folder-safe lower-case kebab-case name, e.g. "pebble-keep".

iso_datetime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, preferably UTC with 'Z', e.g. "2026-10-18T14:05:00Z".

path.description: File path. Use forward slashes and keep it relative to the game project root (e.g. "assets/generated/sprites/golem_t1.png") so the project stays portable across machines and CI.

project_rel_path.description: Strictly project-relative path: no leading '/', no drive letter, no '..' segments. Used where a wrong path would silently defeat enforcement, such as gate evidence (".gamestudio/evidence/F012/static.log").

ratio.description: Fraction between 0 and 1 inclusive (0.42 means 42%). Never use 0-100 percentages in ratio fields.

usd.description: Amount in US dollars, non-negative, decimal (e.g. 0.067).

text_or_list.description: Either one string or a list of strings (bullet points).

platform.description: Target or shipped platform. Mobile projects use "ios" and "android"; the others exist so deconstructions of non-mobile games validate.

orientation.description: Screen orientation. Portrait suits one-handed casual play; landscape suits two-thumb action; "both" doubles UI layout and QA cost.

engine.description: Game engine or runtime. arcosian ships templates for godot and unity.

monetization_model.description: Primary business model: premium (paid up front), iap (free with in-app purchases), ads (ad-funded), hybrid (IAP plus ads, typical for hybrid-casual), subscription.

tier.description: Production stage: prototype (find the fun), slice (vertical slice at target quality), soft_launch (limited-market KPI test), global (worldwide launch), live (operating).

likelihood_impact.description: Qualitative level (low, medium, high) or a 1-5 score where 5 is the most likely / most severe.

verb.description: A player verb: the atomic input-to-intent mapping that mechanics build on.

id.description: Verb id, e.g. "drag_merge", "tap_spawn". Mechanics list these ids in their verbs field.

input.description: Physical input on the device. Suggested vocabulary: tap, double_tap, long_press, drag, swipe, flick, pinch, rotate, hold_release, multi_touch, tilt, virtual_stick, button, none (automatic).

description.description: What the player intends and what the game does in response, in one sentence.

parameter.description: A tunable value of a mechanic or system, with its design range. Balance tools and remote config read these.

key.description: Parameter name, unique within its mechanic, e.g. "spawn_cost". Becomes the remote-config key suffix when the value is tunable live.

value.description: Current design value. Use null while still undecided (TBD); numbers carry the unit in the unit field.

min.description: Lowest value the design tolerates; balance passes and remote config must stay inside [min, max].

note.description: Why this value, what it trades off, and what breaks outside the range.

comparable.description: A reference game and what to take from it. The borrow/change pair forces an explicit transformation instead of a clone.

borrow.description: What we take from it (a mechanic, structure, pacing, feel).

change.description: What we change, and why it serves our players better or differentiates us.

target_audience.description: Who the game is for. Drives tone, difficulty, monetization ethics and store age rating.

age_min.description: Youngest intended player age. Below 13 (or the local digital-consent age) triggers children's-privacy, ad and loot-box constraints; see skill legal-ethics.

segments.description: Player segments in plain words, e.g. "lapsed puzzle players 25-45", "commute players".

motivations.description: Primary player motivations. Use one consistent model, e.g. Quantic Foundry motivation names such as "challenge", "strategy", "completion", "design".

loop_step.description: One node of a loop graph: the player does action, gets reward, and the loop continues at next.

id.description: Step id, unique within its loop, e.g. "s1" or "merge".

action.description: What the player does at this step (verb plus object), e.g. "drag two tier-2 golems together".

reward.description: What the step pays out: a description, a resource map such as {"coins": 40}, or null for a pure decision step.

next.description: Id of the following step, a list of ids for a branch, "loop:<loop-id>" to hand off to another loop, or null to end.

loop.description: A gameplay loop modelled as a graph of steps. Core loops repeat every few seconds; meta loops wrap sessions and days.

type.description: Loop layer: core (moment to moment), meta (progression around sessions), social, monetization, liveops.

period.description: Typical time for one full turn of the loop.

description.description: Why the loop is satisfying and what keeps the player turning it.

steps.description: Steps in play order. The last step's next normally points back to the first, closing the loop.

mechanic.description: A mechanic as listed in the design contract: verbs bound to rules and parameters. A richer stand-alone form is mechanic-card.schema.json.

id.description: Mechanic id, e.g. "merge_two". Referenced by levels (mechanic_refs), cards and features.

category.description: Mechanic family. Suggested vocabulary: movement, aiming, timing, placement, merge, match, sort, physics, combat, resource, construction, chance, collection, progression, social, narrative, puzzle, economy.

verbs.description: Ids of the verbs (contract verbs) this mechanic consumes.

rules.description: Unambiguous rules, one per line, testable by a deterministic playthrough.

feedback.description: Juice and readability: what the player sees, hears and feels when the mechanic fires.

mobile_notes.description: Thumb reach, one-hand play, interruption safety, small-screen readability.

licence.description: Licence and provenance terms of an asset. studio-gateway licence_check compares them with config.revenue; config.licence_allowlist lists terms accepted without review.

terms.description: Licence identifier: an SPDX id for open licences ("CC0-1.0", "CC-BY-4.0") or the provider's terms label or URL for generated assets.

plan_tier.description: Provider plan the asset was generated under (e.g. "free", "starter", "pro"). Free tiers often withhold commercial rights; record it at generation time.

commercial_ok.description: True only if the terms allow use in a commercial game at the project's revenue level.

attribution.description: Required attribution text, or null when none is required.

restrictions.description: Conditions that could invalidate use, e.g. revenue thresholds, no AI training, no resale as a stand-alone asset.

resource_amounts.description: Map of resource id to amount, e.g. {"coins": 40, "stars": 1}. Keys must be resource ids defined in the same document.
